units.text: An address range can be specified by specifying two addresses separated by a comma (⟦0⟧). An address range matches lines starting from where the first address matches, and continues until the second address matches (inclusively):
units.sourceHTML: An address range can be specified by specifying two addresses separated by a comma (,). An address range matches lines starting from where the first address matches, and continues until the second address matches (inclusively):

units.text: If the second address is a ⟦0⟧, then checking for the ending match will start with the line ⟦1⟧following⟦2⟧ the line which matched the first address: a range will always span at least two lines (except of course if the input stream ends).
units.sourceHTML: If the second address is a regexp, then checking for the ending match will start with the line following the line which matched the first address: a range will always span at least two lines (except of course if the input stream ends).

units.text: If the second address is a ⟦0⟧ less than (or equal to) the line matching the first address, then only the one line is matched:
units.sourceHTML: If the second address is a number less than (or equal to) the line matching the first address, then only the one line is matched:

units.text: A line number of ⟦0⟧ can be used in an address specification like ⟦1⟧ so that ⟦2⟧ will try to match ⟦3⟧ in the first input line too. In other words, ⟦4⟧ is similar to ⟦5⟧, except that if ⟦6⟧ matches the very first line of input the ⟦7⟧ form will consider it to end the range, whereas the ⟦8⟧ form will match the beginning of its range and hence make the range span up to the ⟦9⟧second⟦10⟧ occurrence of the regular expression.
units.sourceHTML: A line number of 0 can be used in an address specification like 0,/regexp/ so that sed will try to match regexp in the first input line too. In other words, 0,/regexp/ is similar to 1,/regexp/, except that if addr2 matches the very first line of input the 0,/regexp/ form will consider it to end the range, whereas the 1,/regexp/ form will match the beginning of its range and hence make the range span up to the second occurrence of the regular expression.
